learningObjective: Explain the motivation and dataflow of disaggregated prefill/decode serving.

canonicalClaims.claim: Disaggregated serving places prefill and decode on separate GPU pools because prefill is compute-bound and decode is memory-bandwidth bound; separation avoids mutual interference and allows independent hardware provisioning per phase, at the cost of a KV cache transfer between pools per request.
conditions: Workload has mixed prefill and decode phases.
nonImplications: Does not imply disaggregation always wins; short prompts may not benefit.
Does not imply model or precision splitting.

misconceptions.claim: Disaggregation runs different models for prefill and decode.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Same model runs on both pools; only the phase is split.

misconceptions.claim: Disaggregation is a security isolation design.
Prefill and decode use different numerical precision on different hardware in disaggregation.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Both phases typically run in FP16/BF16; precision is not the split.

implementationFacts: Per-request KV transfer between pools is the main new communication step; typically over NVLink or InfiniBand RDMA.
DistServe and SplitWise reported large TPOT-latency improvements under mixed load.
performanceScenarios: Disaggregation shines when prefill-decode workload mix varies over time and per-pool scaling is beneficial.
The transfer cost is bounded by the size of the prompt's KV cache, which is manageable with high-bandwidth interconnects.
